data.long_meaning: The name Damariana is of Hebrew origin, derived from the Hebrew word 'damar' which means 'to quiet, to subdue, to tame'. The name is often interpreted as 'beloved' or 'dear one'. In the Bible, the name Damar is found in the Old Testament and is borne by a man who was a friend of King Hezekiah of Judah (2 Kings 18:21). This name has been used in Christian tradition as a feminine given name, imbuing it with the same sense of love and devotion.

The name is derived from the Damar people's name for their land, which was 'Taparigua de la Costa' or 'Coastal Land of Taparigua'.

historical_references.reference: Damariana was also known as the 'Islands of the Damaras' in the late 18th and early 19th centuries, referring to a group of islands off the coast of present-day Venezuela that were part of the Dutch colony of Curaçao.
